The table spec

Source: vignettes/articles/table-spec.Rmd
table-spec.Rmd

The table spec says how an ARD becomes a table: which keys go across and down, the label and order of each variable, the template and digits of each cell, the pages, the column widths, the header. It stands for an rtfreporter plan: table_plan() with the roles, and one plan_*() verb for each thing the other sheets say.

  • tfl_table_code(spec) writes that plan as code – the program a study keeps, which no longer reads the workbook;
  • tfl_table_plan(data, spec) builds the same plan from an ARD.
library(tflspec)
library(rtfreporter)

The sheets

One sheet per grain, so each fact is written once. Column names are rtfreporter’s argument names: a layout column is the verb’s prefix and its argument (pages_max_rows is plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = )).

Sheet One row per Goes to
study study fact rounding, output_path, program_dir
tables table table_plan(cols, rows, label), plan_cells(), plan_sort()
variables variable plan_labels(), plan_levels()
codelists value of a variable, of a report the ARD’s factors (its values the labels), then plan_levels()
cells line of a cell plan_cells(), plan_digits()
digits statistic the decimals of {mean}, {sd}, {p} … in every template that says none
layout table plan_paginate_rows(), plan_row_group(), plan_blanks(), plan_stub(), plan_paginate_cols()
columns printed column plan_columns(), plan_hide()
style table plan_style()
cell_styles styling plan_cell_style()
col_header header cell plan_col_header()

The output_id rule: a row with a blank output_id is the study’s default; a report’s own row replaces it, per sheet (and, on the keyed sheets, per key). The exception is codelists, which has no defaults: every row names its report. Every column is described on its header cell’s comment in the workbook and by tfl_spec_columns().

The example workbooks

The package comes with the specs of five tables – demographics (DM), adverse events by SOC and PT (AE), response by subgroup (ORR), a lab shift table (LB) and PK concentrations (PK) – each in its own workbook, and all five in study.xlsx:

ex <- system.file("extdata", "ard-spec", package = "tflspec")
spec <- tfl_read_table_spec(file.path(ex, "study.xlsx"))
spec$tables[, c("output_id", "cols", "rows", "label", "sort")]
#>   output_id              cols
#> 1        DM            TRT01A
#> 2        AE      TRT01A | SEX
#> 3       ORR TRT01A | variable
#> 4        LB            BGRADE
#> 5        PK           NOMTIME
#>                                                    rows                  label
#> 1                                      group = variable                   <NA>
#> 2                                     group1 = AEBODSYS        label = AEDECOD
#> 3             family = group2 | subgroup = group2_level                     NA
#> 4 PARAM = PARAM | group1 = "Worst grade after baseline"         label = .label
#> 5                                     Analyte = ANALYTE Statistic = stat_label
#>                                      sort
#> 1                                    <NA>
#> 2 .overall | group1 | .depth | -n | label
#> 3                                   FALSE
#> 4                                    <NA>
#> 5                                    <NA>

The AE table: treatment groups across, SOC as row groups, PT as rows, sorted by frequency.

cat(tfl_table_code(spec, "AE", pipe = "|>"), sep = "\n")
# the code lists: each value in its order, as the table shows it
cl_trt01a <- c("Drug X", "Control")
cl_sex <- c("F", "M")

plan <- ard |>
  normalize_ard(hierarchy = c("AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD")) |>
  table_plan(
    cols = c("TRT01A", "SEX"),
    rows = c(group1 = "AEBODSYS"),
    label = c(label = "AEDECOD")
  ) |>
  plan_cells(default = "{n:.0f} ({p:.1f%})") |>
  plan_levels(TRT01A = cl_trt01a, SEX = cl_sex) |>
  plan_digits(rounding = "sas") |>
  plan_sort(c(".overall", "group1", ".depth", "-n", "label")) |>
  plan_col_header(
    data.frame(
      line = c("1", "1", "2", "2"),
      cols = c("row_label", ".values", "row_label", ".values"),
      span = c(NA, "TRT01A", NA, "each"),
      text = c(
        NA_character_,
        "{col1} (N={n:sum})",
        "System organ class\n  Preferred term",
        "{col2}\n(N={n})\nn (%)"
      ),
      border_bottom = c(NA, "single", NA, NA)
    )
  ) |>
  plan_stub(name = "row_label", before = TRUE) |>
  plan_blanks(
    where = "between_groups",
    first = TRUE,
    last = TRUE,
    counted = TRUE
  ) |>
  plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = 28, split = "group_force") |>
  plan_columns(widths = c(row_label = 36, .values = 8)) |>
  plan_style(align_count_pct = TRUE, row_height_twips = 220)

Cells

cells rows are templates: {mean} ({sd}), {n} ({p:.1f%}). A row with a blank variable is the table’s default template. Rows with the same variable / context / row form one chain tried in order, and when is an R guard (n == 0). In a table of one statistic per row (tables$stats = rows), a row with no template gives one statistic’s digits.

spec$cells[spec$cells$output_id %in% "ORR",
           c("variable", "row", "when", "template")]
#>    variable row          when                            template
#> 6         n   1          <NA>                             {N:.0f}
#> 7      resp   1        n == 0                                   0
#> 8      resp   1 estimate == 1                       {n:.0f} (100)
#> 9      resp   1          <NA>           {n:.0f} ({estimate:.1f%})
#> 10     resp   2          <NA> [{conf.low:.1f%}, {conf.high:.1f%}]

Numbers or the ARD’s text: tables$value

tables$value says which of the ARD’s values a table prints:

  • stat (the default): the numbers, rounded here – by the digits sheet below, or a template’s own format ({mean:.1f});
  • stat_fmt: the ARD’s own text, as the ARD program formatted it (analyses$formats); nothing is rounded here, and a template still puts two in one cell ({mean} ({sd})).

A template may say otherwise for one value: {mean:stat_fmt}, {mean:.2f}.

A Total column

A column for all subjects comes from cards’ own overall rows, not from a group the data does not have. On the analyses sheet, overall = TRUE runs the analysis again without its by and binds it under the grouped one; on the tables sheet, total is the column’s heading (Total) and total_position puts it last (the default) or first. The table is written with rtfreporter’s plan_total(), whose (N={n}) is the study total. In the ARS the analysis is written twice, by its groups and over all subjects.

Decimals, written once: the digits sheet

The digits sheet gives each statistic’s decimals once, for every analysis variable (variable blank), and a variable’s exceptions (a variable named). They are written into the templates’ tokens that say no format: {mean} ({sd}) becomes {mean:.1f} ({sd:.2f}). A template’s own format, or a cells row’s digits, wins.

A report’s code lists, and the variables’ labels

A report’s codelists rows say what each value is in the data its program makes: the ARD program puts the labels on the data (see The ARD spec), so the ARD already holds “Female”, and the table only orders the ARD’s values (plan_levels(), in the labels). A variable’s heading is the variables sheet’s label (plan_labels()). The code list of variable (an earlier form of the headings) is moved to the variables sheet’s label when the table spec is read, with a message. Labels are a report’s, like the rest of its code lists.

adsl <- adsl[adsl$SAFFL == "Y", ]    # the sample study's ADSL, safety set
adsl$SEX <- factor(adsl$SEX, c("F", "M"), c("Female", "Male"))  # as set_levels()
ard2 <- cards::ard_stack(
  adsl, .by = TRT01A,
  cards::ard_summary(variables = AGE),
  cards::ard_tabulate(variables = c(SEX, AGEGR1)))
df <- function(...) data.frame(..., stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
sp <- tfl_table_spec(list(
  tables = df(output_id = "T-DM", cols = "TRT01A", rows = "group = variable"),
  variables = df(output_id = "T-DM", variable = c("AGE", "SEX", "AGEGR1"),
                 order = 1:3, label = c("Age (years)", "Sex", "Age group")),
  codelists = df(output_id = "T-DM", variable = "SEX", value = c("F", "M"),
                 label = c("Female", "Male"), order = 1:2),
  cells = df(output_id = "T-DM", variable = c("continuous", "categorical"),
             row = c("Mean (SD)", NA), template = c("{mean} ({sd})", "{n} ({p})")),
  digits = df(output_id = "T-DM", statistic = c("mean", "sd", "p"),
              digits = c(1, 2, 1))))
cat(tfl_table_code(sp, "T-DM", pipe = "|>"), sep = "\n")
# the code lists: each value in its order, as the table shows it
cl_sex <- c("Female", "Male")

plan <- ard |>
  normalize_ard() |>
  table_plan(cols = "TRT01A", rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
  plan_cells(
    continuous = list("Mean (SD)" = "{mean:.1f} ({sd:.2f})"),
    categorical = "{n} ({p:.1f%})"
  ) |>
  plan_labels(AGE = "Age (years)", SEX = "Sex", AGEGR1 = "Age group") |>
  plan_levels(variable = c("AGE", "SEX", "AGEGR1"), SEX = cl_sex)
knitr::kable(plan_apply(tfl_table_plan(normalize_ard(ard2), sp, output_id = "T-DM") |>
                          plan_cells(notes = FALSE), stage = "table"))
group label Drug X Control
Age (years) Mean (SD) 60.1 (9.59) 62.7 (9.76)
Sex Female 41 (51.2) 30 (38.5)
Sex Male 39 (48.8) 48 (61.5)
Age group <65 57 (71.2) 44 (56.4)
Age group >=65 23 (28.7) 34 (43.6)

From an ARD: a template to start from

tfl_table_spec_template() walks an ARD and writes the tables, variables and cells sheets – the variables with their levels, a template for each kind of row – to be edited:

ard <- cards::ard_stack(
  adsl, .by = TRT01A,
  cards::ard_summary(variables = AGE),
  cards::ard_tabulate(variables = AGEGR1))
tmpl <- tfl_table_spec_template(ard, cols = "TRT01A", output_id = "T-DM")
tmpl$variables
#>   output_id variable  label order     levels empty_levels under
#> 1      T-DM      AGE    AGE     1       <NA>         <NA>  <NA>
#> 2      T-DM   AGEGR1 AGEGR1     2 <65 | >=65         <NA>  <NA>
tmpl$cells[, c("variable", "row", "template")]
#>   variable       row      template
#> 1      AGE         n           {N}
#> 2      AGE Mean (SD) {mean} ({sd})
#> 3      AGE    Median      {median}
#> 4      AGE  Min, Max  {min}, {max}
#> 5   AGEGR1      <NA>     {n} ({p})

Write it with tfl_write_table_spec(tmpl, "spec/tables.xlsx"), edit it in Excel, read it back with tfl_read_table_spec().

A plan, and one report’s own change

tfl_table_plan() returns a plan, so any rtfreporter verb piped after it wins over the workbook (“last wins”) – one report departs from the study’s workbook in one line, and the workbook is not touched:

plan <- tfl_table_plan(normalize_ard(ard), tmpl) |>
  plan_cells(notes = FALSE) |>
  plan_labels(AGE = "Age (years)", AGEGR1 = "Age group, n (%)")
knitr::kable(plan_apply(plan, stage = "table"))
group label Drug X Control
Age (years) n 80 78
Age (years) Mean (SD) 60.1 (9.6) 62.7 (9.8)
Age (years) Median 59.5 62.5
Age (years) Min, Max 39.0, 82.0 42.0, 85.0
Age group, n (%) <65 57 (71.3) 44 (56.4)
Age group, n (%) >=65 23 (28.8) 34 (43.6)

A plan written in code, back to a workbook

tfl_as_table_spec() goes the other way: a plan written in code becomes a workbook. It compares the RTF the two make (byte by byte) and lists what a sheet cannot carry (attr(, "not_converted")) – a look computed row by row, a step after the pages are made – which stays in code, after the plan:

coded <- table_plan(normalize_ard(ard), cols = "TRT01A",
                    rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
  plan_cells(continuous = c("Mean (SD)" = "{mean} ({sd})"),
             categorical = "{n} ({p:.1f%})", notes = FALSE) |>
  plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = 30)
back <- tfl_as_table_spec(coded, output_id = "T-DM")
back$cells[, c("variable", "row", "template")]
#>      variable       row       template
#> 1  continuous Mean (SD)  {mean} ({sd})
#> 2 categorical      <NA> {n} ({p:.1f%})
#> 3         AGE Mean (SD)  {mean} ({sd})
#> 4      AGEGR1      <NA> {n} ({p:.1f%})
back$layout[, "pages_max_rows", drop = FALSE]
#>   pages_max_rows
#> 1             30

Reports and several workbooks

A table spec is usually read together with its report spec (the page, titles, footnotes): tfl_read_report_spec(c("report.xlsx", "tables.xlsx"), output_id = ) reads both, and one object serves tfl_table_plan() and tfl_report() alike. A sheet may be in any of the workbooks given, but in only one. See Reports.
